idiom_name: one coarse boundary component per use-case cluster (class, module or package) over injected fine-grained services, with the unit of work at the coarse operation
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define one boundary component per use-case cluster and give it one operation per conversation; its collaborators are the fine-grained services, business objects or repositories, supplied by constructor, function parameter or composition root - never looked up from inside. The component sequences the calls, validates input, applies authorization, translates failures into stable application errors, and owns the unit of work (one transaction per coarse operation). Business rules stay in the collaborators: the facade orchestrates the use case, it does not implement it. Keep the component stateless unless the conversation itself must survive between calls; a stateful form then needs an explicit scope, expiry and cleanup rule. Data crossing the boundary travels as a coarse payload (Transfer Object) rather than as domain entities.
code_sketch:
client -> facade.placeOrder(req)            # one coarse operation per conversation
  facade:  validate(req); authorize(client, req)
           quote   = pricing.quote(...)     # fine-grained collaborators, injected
           reserve = inventory.reserve(...)
           order   = repo.insert(...)       # all inside one unit of work
  facade:  translate(domain errors) -> application errors; return coarse payload
pitfalls: Letting the boundary component implement business rules instead of orchestrating collaborators; that path leads to the god facade and duplicated logic across facades.
Passing domain entities across the boundary, so clients lazily navigate the object graph and the coarse contract leaks.
Choosing the facade method as the transaction boundary and then performing remote or slow I/O inside it.
A stateful boundary component without an explicit lifetime, expiry and cleanup rule.

Wrong move: catching a domain exception around a participant that already marked the shared transaction rollback-only -> failure: the facade's error-translation path reaches commit and the container throws UnexpectedRollbackException instead of the graceful fallback -> instead: let the exception propagate so the boundary rollback is honest, or give that participant REQUIRES_NEW (or bean-managed transactions) if the workflow genuinely continues past its failure.

Wrong move: exposing the facade through a remote business interface when every client lives in the same JVM -> failure: each coarse call pays pass-by-copy serialization on arguments and results, so the boundary that exists to remove per-call overhead adds it back -> instead: use a local (or no-interface) view for in-JVM callers and a remote interface only for clients that actually cross the JVM.

Wrong move: pinning a stateful facade's conversation to one node with no passivation or replication story -> failure: a node restart kills every in-flight conversation and, under load, the per-client instance pool grows until the heap is exhausted -> instead: keep conversation state in the database or a shared store behind a stateless facade, or configure passivation, session timeouts and stateful replication before scaling out.
